name: Pumba
what_it_is: Pumba is a chaos testing and network emulation CLI tool for Docker and containerd containers. It can kill, stop, pause, or remove containers, inject network faults (delay, loss, corruption, rate-limiting) via Linux tc/netem and iptables, and stress-test CPU/memory/IO using stress-ng.
components: Helper/sidecar nettools container (shares target network namespace for tc/iptables injection)
pumba-alpine-nettools image (ghcr.io/alexei-led/pumba-alpine-nettools) — iproute2 + iptables on Alpine
pumba-debian-nettools image (ghcr.io/alexei-led/pumba-debian-nettools) — iproute2 + iptables on Debian
protocols: Any (tc/netem operates at network namespace level, protocol-agnostic for egress)
netem (Linux kernel traffic control — delay, loss, corrupt, duplicate, rate)
measurement: No built-in metrics export; chaos effects are observed on the target application
Delay: configurable time (ms) + jitter (ms) + correlation (%) + distribution (uniform/normal/pareto/paretonormal)
Loss: percentage (0-100) with optional correlation; also 4-state Markov (loss-state) and Gilbert-Elliot (loss-gemodel) models
Rate: bandwidth in kbit/mbit units with optional packet overhead and cell size parameters
configuration: --random: select one random container from matched set
--duration: how long the network chaos rule is active (required for netem/iptables commands)
Container selection: by name, name regex (re2: prefix), or Docker labels
fault_injection: netem delay: add egress latency with optional jitter, correlation, and statistical distribution
netem loss: drop egress packets by Bernoulli probability
netem loss-state: bursty egress loss via 4-state Markov model
netem loss-gemodel: egress loss via Gilbert-Elliot good/bad state channel model
netem duplicate: duplicate egress packets by probability
netem corrupt: corrupt egress packet bits by probability
iptables loss: drop ingress packets (random or nth-packet matching)
kill: send signal to PID 1 of container (default SIGKILL)
stop: docker stop / containerd task stop
exec: run arbitrary command inside container
stress: CPU / memory / IO stress via stress-ng (child or same-cgroup injection)
modes: Recurring: use --interval to repeat chaos at fixed intervals
Random targeting: --random picks one container from matched set each interval
Docker runtime mode (default): uses Docker API; network chaos via sidecar sharing network namespace
containerd runtime mode: uses containerd API directly; network chaos via exec inside target container (requires tc/iptables in image, or --tc-image sidecar)
constraints: netem rules apply to EGRESS traffic only; iptables rules apply to INGRESS traffic only — combined use required for bidirectional fault injection
Network chaos on Docker requires NET_ADMIN capability on the helper container and access to the host Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock)
containerd network chaos requires tc/iptables installed inside the target container image unless --tc-image sidecar is used
stress-ng must be available in the container (or injected via the stress command's cgroup options)
--duration must be shorter than --interval when using recurring mode
Container filtering by label is Docker-only; containerd mode requires container ID or name
docker_services: pumba (CLI) — run as: docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ghcr.io/alexei-led/pumba:latest
pumba-alpine-nettools — sidecar helper image used automatically via --tc-image flag
pumba-debian-nettools — alternative Debian-based sidecar helper image
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository — pumba is a standalone CLI tool, not a composed service
No built-in metrics or observability endpoint (Prometheus, etc.)
No web UI or REST API — CLI only
No native Windows or macOS network chaos support (netem/iptables are Linux kernel features)
No HTTP-layer fault injection (operates at L3/L4 only)
